models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign, near-calm pattern over the Aeolians - winds under 7 kt and seas under 1 ft through the current model horizon.
briefing.synopsis: No organised pressure gradient over the southern Tyrrhenian in any run: ECMWF IFS 0.25° (01 Oct 18Z), ECMWF AIFS (02 Oct 00Z) and ICON-2i (02 Oct 00Z) all show light, rotating winds of roughly 2-5 kt across the island group, swinging from an overnight S/SE land breeze to N/NE by midday. Seas are essentially flat - MFWAM (01 Oct 12Z) and ECMWF WAM (01 Oct 18Z) agree on total wave and swell of 0.1-0.5 ft everywhere. If this held, the week would be a motoring and gentle-reaching week rather than a sailing one, with anchorage choice dictated by scenery rather than shelter. The payload carries no synoptic chart, so I can't name the feature responsible beyond saying the gradient is absent.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the night of 03 Oct at Portorosa the recommended berth is Portorosa Marina - an enclosed basin with all-round shelter, scored sheltered at 1.0.
